part.text:
`/api/manufacturers/ratings` returns `[{"manufacturer":"Mitsubishi","rating":3.5},{"manufacturer":"Honda","rating":3.0}]`.

Note: "rating":3.0 — the e2e ReportStepDefs does `Double.valueOf(getCellText(...))` so the text must be parseable as a double: "3.0" or "3" both parse. GWT NumberCell renders 3.0 as "3"? Actually GWT NumberCell uses `NumberFormat.getDecimalFormat()` by default... The report average check: `almostEqual(average, referenceAverage, 0.001)` where average = Double.valueOf(cellText). If I render "3.0" that parses to 3.0. Fine. If I render "3" also fine.

Also note the average check iterates over report rows; for each manufacturer in report table, `averages.get(manufacturer)` must exist (else NPE). The averages map is built from the rating page rows: car text like "Honda/Accord" → manufacturer = substring before '/'. So the "Car" column text must contain the manufacturer name followed by '/' and the model. The RatingDto.toString() gives `manufacturer.getName() + "/" + car.getModel()`, e.g. "Honda/Accord".

So in my rating table, the "Car" column should display "Honda/Accord" format. The manufacturer substring is `car.substring(0, car.indexOf('/'))`.

Now, the ratings list order — the e2e iterates over all rating rows on the rating page and computes averages, then compares to the report. Both come from the same datastore, so consistent.

part.text:
The Rating domain stores a Ref<Car>. When creating from a RatingDto, `Rating.create(ratingDto)` presumably does `Car.create(carDto)` — let me check what happens when saving a rating whose car only has an id. Objectify `Ref.create(Car.create(dto))` where Car.create probably sets id. Actually, safest approach: send the full car object (as the GWT client does — the ValueListBox holds full CarDto objects from getCars()). Let me test POST /api/ratings with a full car object.

Also I should check RatingResourceImpl for saveOrCreate. Actually simplest: test it with curl, mimicking what my Angular app will send.

**REPRODUCED!!!** Even in isolation:

```
resolved via factory inject(): default
resolved via get(): default
```

The explicit `{provide: Token, useClass: Sub}` LOSES to the token's own `ɵprov` factory (`providedIn: 'root'`, `useFactory`)! But wait — the deprecation warning says "DI is instantiating a token 'Sub' that inherits its @Injectable decorator" — so Sub IS being instantiated... but then `whoami()` returns 'default'?!

OH. MY. GOD. I SEE IT NOW!!! **`Sub` inherits `Token.ɵprov` — and `Token.ɵprov.factory = () => new DefaultImpl()`!** When the injector instantiates the `useClass: Sub` provider, it uses **Sub's inherited ɵprov.factory** — which creates a **DefaultImpl**!! That's the "inherits its @Injectable decorator" mechanism: for a Type provider, R3Injector looks at the class's injectable def (ɵprov) to get its factory — and the inherited ɵprov's factory creates the PARENT'S configured implementation (DefaultImpl)!!

So `{provide: UrlSerializer, useClass: GwtUrlSerializer}` → R3Injector resolves the useClass by using GwtUrlSerializer's ɵprov — INHERITED from UrlSerializer — whose factory is `() => new DefaultUrlSerializer()`. Result: DefaultUrlSerializer, NOT my serializer. My class's CONSTRUCTOR is never even called. That's exactly what we observed (counters null, resolved class = DefaultUrlSerializer)!

THAT's the bug in my approach! The fix: don't extend UrlSerializer — OR add my own @Injectable() to GwtUrlSerializer so it gets its OWN ɵprov/factory.

Options:
1. Add `@Injectable()` to GwtUrlSerializer — gives it its own ɵprov (no providedIn, just a factory that news up the class) → `{provide: UrlSerializer, useClass: GwtUrlSerializer}` then instantiates MY class properly. ✓ (The deprecation warning even tells us this!)

2. Implement the serializer as an object: `{ provide: UrlSerializer, useValue: customSerializerInstance }` where customSerializer is a plain object with parse/serialize methods — no class inheritance issue at all.

Option 1 is cleanest Angular-wise:

```typescript
@Injectable()
export class GwtUrlSerializer extends UrlSerializer { ... }
```

That gives GwtUrlSerializer its own ɵprov → the useClass provider uses ITS factory → new GwtUrlSerializer() → my methods run.

Wait — but does @Injectable() on a subclass produce a proper ɵprov? Yes: ɵɵngDeclareInjectable({token: GwtUrlSerializer}) hmm — the token would be GwtUrlSerializer itself... For useClass providers, R3Injector's providerDef: `provider.useClass` → gets injectable def of the class → factory. With @Injectable(), the def exists with a default factory (construct via ɵfac reflection). ✓

## What was built

The Angular 18 app under `src/app/` (standalone components, strict TS), mirroring the GWT screens one-for-one:

| GWT source | Angular |
|---|---|

| `RatingView`/`EditRatingView` | `rating/` — table `gwt-debug-ratings` (ID/Car/Rating/Delete), Car cell renders `Manufacturer/Model` (`RatingDto.toString()`), create form loads cars first (`ratingInput`/`ratingSave`), confirm before delete |
| `ReportView` | `report/` — table `gwt-debug-reports` (Manufacturer/Rating) |
| `NameTokens`/`DebugIds`/DTOs/JAX-RS resources | `name-tokens.ts`, `debug-ids.ts`, `core/dto.ts`, `core/api-paths.ts`, `core/api.service.ts` (only real endpoints: `/api/manufacturers[/ratings|/{id}]`, `/api/ratings`, `/api/cars?offset=0&limit=-1`, `/api/session`) |
